notes: 0.2.0: the match sheets (duels.php, Read the scorecards - matches): one sheet a match, its two cards side by side, for individual and team brackets and round robins. The round being shot is chosen first (as the core's scorecard printouts list them, narrowed to today's and those not finished), its matches fetched with their formats from the events' settings (sets or points, ends, arrows, shoot-off). The cards are fitted with the match card's layout (duel-layout.js); the match is told by the sheet's barcode, else by the names above the cards, the event under them and the round in the table's title, against the round's matches. Every cell is read: arrows, end or set totals, running totals, the set point circled or written over, the running set points, the total, the shoot-off, the closest and winner boxes; a cell without ink reads blank. Each card's arrows are chosen by its sums, then the match is worked out from both cards and checked against what was circled, written and ticked; an end ianseo holds in another order counts as the same. Import the data writes both sides through the core's UpdateArrowString or RobinUpdateArrowString; Validate the data confirms the match as the barcode check's CONFIRM does (the winner moved on, a round robin's group ranked again). Automatic and manual camera modes, or a picture imported. The reading pages share their HTML (lib/page.php) and their script, the duel page's own part given as an adaptation (duel.js). The page Cells to check shows the cells of every competition, whichever is open, and the training set's arrows whose label is not sure, each with where it comes from and why. The reading networks are trained again, the same for both pages, on qualification and match sheets (those printed by older ianseo versions too, their running total in sets: duel-layout.js option direct), from sure labels only: an arrow the database does not tell for sure (X or 10, an end entered in another order than the sheet's, a value the reading does not see) is learnt as checked on that page, left out while it is not. On the qualification photos, arrows shown sure and wrong 17 to 14, cards read all right 663 to 691; no silent error on the synthetic sheets. On a competition left out of that training, 97.9 % of the match arrows right (96.7 % before the checks). Measured on 180 scanned match pages of five competitions: 96.5 to 99.2 % of the arrows right, set points 95 to 99 %, winner boxes 97 to 100 %. The network reading a written number whole is trained again with the checked cells: on cells it never saw, 83.3 to 85.6 % of the numbers right.
